newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2945 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2926, depressed by word of central bank sales that triggered some follow-up selling late in the session.
Tbe weighted average price on Monday was 8.2921.
Dealers said that as the currency's rise was capped at about 8.2920, speculative selling together with possible central bank intervention put heavy downward pressure on the yuan.
The yuan opened up at an intraday high of 8.2921 and moved in a narrow range between 8.2921 and 8.2925 for most of the session, before slipping in late trading.
Trading was more active than Tuesday with most business done at the 8.2928 level, dealers said.
"When the central bank got involved, dollar buying emerged to depress the yuan's rising trend," said one dealer.
A second dealer said the general feeling of the market was that the yuan was due for a correction, according to technical analysis and the central bank's will.
"With such expectations, the yuan can only be expected to fall," he said.
